evidence_timeline.summary: Following the detection of the sub-solar mass merger candidate S251112cm (the LIGO-Virgo-Kagra Collaboration, GCN 42650), we conducted follow-up observations focused on the northern region of the initial bayestar skymap (GCN 42650) using the newly deployed 2.5-meter Wide Field Survey Telescope (WFST Collaboration; Wang et al., 2023) at the Lenghu Astronomical Observation Base (Qinghai province, China). Observations began at UTC 2025-11-13T11:29:36, corresponding to ~20.2 hours after the merger event (UTC 2025-11-12T15:18:45). The follow-ups lasted for three nights until UTC 2025-11-15T23:16:16. We observed in WFST g, r, and i bands with exposure times of 45-90 seconds. A total area of about 727.4 square degrees of the 90% skymap (GCN 42650) was observed, covering ~64% of the event localization. Additionally, ~7.5% skymap was covered in 30s g- and r-band exposures through the WFST wide-field survey (WFS) 6.35 hours after the merger event. The follow-up observation data were processed using the WFST pipeline. For images localized in WFS, image subtraction was performed using the WFST stacking images taken berfore the event as templates. The search for the counterpart of S251112cm was performed mainly through visual inspection based on the locations of nearby galaxies, considering the distance estimate of 93 +/- 27 Mpc (redshift ~ 0.02; the LIGO-Virgo-Kagra Collaboration, GCN 42690) and the uncertainty of the potential electromagnetic counterpart. All extragalactic transient candidates detected by WFST during follow-ups were reported to the IAU Transient Name Server (TNS). After excluding sources with pre-merger detections reported in TNS, only one candidate was found to be located near a galaxy with spectroscopic redshift below 0.045: AT2025aebp was first detected at 60992.93 (+1.3 days post-merger) with 21.5 +/- 0.1 mag in r-band, and the spectroscopic redshift of its possible host galaxy SDSS J103703.20+231142.2 is 0.043. Additionally, we report three other sources without pre-merger detections. rules.photometry: Only exactly compatible photometry (same epoch, band, system, method, calibration and direct/difference state, two or more providers) is compared. The limiting magnitude or flux that a provider reports alongside a detection is that epoch's detection threshold, not a non-detection, and is not compared with the detection; a detection brighter than another provider's non-detection limit at the same epoch is a status conflict. A group is listed only when it is still inconsistent under these rules; at most 10 groups per event, most significant first.
rules.position: Two positions with no stated uncertainty are inconsistent when they are more than 2 arcsec apart; when one states an error radius, the separation is compared with 3 times that radius.
rules.redshift: Two redshifts with no stated uncertainty are inconsistent when they differ by more than 0.005 (about 1,500 km/s); transient and host redshifts are different definitions and are listed, not compared; host redshifts of differently named hosts are an identity ambiguity.
rules.revision: A retracted row, or a superseded row of the same provider whose value differs beyond the property's rule, is a revision or retraction; a revision within the rule is consistent; the earlier value stays visible.
rules.sigma: Two values that both state an uncertainty are inconsistent when they differ by more than 3 combined standard deviations (uncertainties added in quadrature; a stated position error radius is treated as one standard deviation).

runs.claimBoundary: A ranking of retained catalogued galaxies under stated priors; the most probable candidate is a suggestion for follow-up, not a host identification, and a host fainter than the catalogues or outside their cones is always possible.

rules.missed: a host not in the retained catalogues counts as one candidate at f = missedFractionalOffset
rules.offset: f = separation / directional light radius (SIMBAD shape), else separation x kpc/arcsec(z) / physical scale, else separation / angular scale; term exp(-f); f > maxFractionalOffset gives 0
rules.probable: the top candidate is 'probable' when its posterior >= probablePosterior and >= probableRatio x the next hypothesis
rules.redshift: only when the transient and the candidate both have a redshift: exp(-0.5 (dz / sigma)^2), sigma^2 = sum of the stated errors^2 + floor^2

warnings: some candidates have neither a retained shape nor a redshift; their offsets use the stated angular scale
the transient has no retained redshift; the redshift term was not used

runs.claimBoundary: Retained earlier detections at the position; they show earlier variability at the position, not that the same source caused both.
runs.notComputedReason: no retained photometry more than 30 days before discovery

parameters.rule: prior activity = at least minDetections detections (S/N >= 5) on at least minNights nights more than gapDays before discovery
